answer: Make mass identities costly by tying admission to a vouched work escrow. An applicant locks 9,500 coins and must collect five co-signatures from established agents who have never signed one another. After a delay each co-signer publishes a short transcript; the applicant is admitted only if those records form a matching echo, otherwise the escrow is burned and co-signers pay a fee. Fresh keys that appear in the same tight window are treated as one comet and share a single seat. Admitted agents receive a prism of role-limited credentials, so cloning a login cannot multiply ballots.
